new_statements.quote: Guthrie (1948) によるバントゥ諸語の参照番号は F12 であり、相互理解が可能な近接の言語に F11 のトングェ語がある。多くの話者が、両言語は兄弟関係にあり非常に近いという。…ベンデ語の声調は、決して例は多くないが、語彙的および文法的弁別機能を持つ。音節ごとに高声調 H(igh)、低声調 L(ow)、上昇声調 R(ising)、下降声調 F(alling) の 4 種類の実現声調がある…ベンデ語の声調は、音節数が増えてもパターンが限定的であり、基本的には 3 パターンである。すなわち、(a) 語幹がすべて H、(b) 接頭辞は H で語幹が L あるいは R ではじまるもの、(c) は接頭辞が L で語幹の次末音節に H ないし H を含む R や F が現れるものである。
new_statements.translation: Its Guthrie (1948) reference number is F12, and a neighbouring, mutually intelligible language is Tongwe, F11. Many speakers say the two languages are siblings and very close. ... Bende tone, though examples are by no means numerous, has lexical and grammatical distinctive function. Each syllable carries one of four surface tones: High, Low, Rising, Falling ... Bende tone patterns remain limited even as syllable count increases; basically there are three: (a) stem all H; (b) prefix H with the stem beginning in L or R; (c) prefix L with H (or an R/F containing H) appearing on the penultimate syllable of the stem.
new_statements.citation: 阿部優子 [Abe, Yuko]. 2021. ベンデ語の声調 [Tone in Bende]. In 梶茂樹 (ed.), アフリカ諸語の声調・アクセント [Tone and Accent in African Languages], ch.12, pp. 249-278. Tokyo: ILCAA, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
new_statements.locator: sec. 1, p. 249 (pdf p. 1); pattern summary repeated sec. 5, p. 272
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: extracted text of p.249 (pdf p.1, sec.1 'ベンデ語の背景') contains every clause of the quoted Japanese verbatim; the '…' marks cover two omitted stretches (speaker-count sentence + scope sentence; 'があるが、本稿では…その結果、'). The (a)/(b)/(c) three-pattern summary recurs verbatim on p.272 (sec.5 intro) as the locator says. Translation is faithful. I also a full-text search for stress/accent the whole chapter for アクセント/強勢/ストレス/stress/accent: the only hit is the project title in fn.1 ('声調・アクセントの総合的研究'); the chapter never characterises Bende (let alone Tongwe) in stress/accent terms, so 'tone language, no stress statement' is the right reading OF THIS SOURCE. Nakamura et al. 2017 p.222 (tong1320/)…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only first-hand prosodic description is of the Bende variety (bend1258), which Abe treats as one language with Tongwe: a restricted tone system with lexically assigned tonal types (H, L, 0), where one class surfaces with H on the stem penult; nothing is said about word stress, and no phonological study of Tongwe proper exists (Nakamura et al. 2017: 222, saved in tong1320/).
new_statements.exceptions: Abe notes R and F surface tones are positionally restricted (sec. 3.3) and that phrase/sentence tone is uninvestigated; loan-type (0) words pattern with penult H per the 2006 thesis abstract summary. None of this is stated for Tongwe itself.
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms of nouns and verbal gerunds (引用形); phrase-level tone explicitly not studied. Statement applies to Bende (F12) data from Katavi Region, not to Tongwe (F11) speech.
new_statements.identity_note: No phonological description of Tongwe proper (tong1320, F11) exists; Nakamura et al. 2017: 222 say so explicitly. The quoted statement describes Bende (bend1258, F12), which Abe (2006 thesis; 2021) defines as one language with Tongwe ('two varieties of one language', mutually intelligible). Glottolog and ISO keep them apart (tny vs bdp). Any catalog entry built from Abe would be a Bende entry, not a Tongwe one.

sources.note: Describes BENDE (F12), stating Tongwe (F11) is a mutually intelligible neighbouring language. Bende tone has lexical and grammatical distinctive function; surface H, L, R, F per syllable; citation-form words fall into three patterns: (a) all-H stem, (b) H prefix + stem beginning L/R, (c) L prefix with H (or R/F containing H) on the stem penult. No statement about word stress/accent; phrase-level tone not investigated.

sources.citation: Abe, Yuko. 2006. A descriptive study of Bende phonology and morphology (Bantu F.12, Tanzania). PhD thesis, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (English abstract; body is scanned Japanese without text layer).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: English abstract: the introduction 'defines Bende and Tongwe as two varieties of one language'; ch.3: 'Tone is a distinctive feature for Bende phonology. Each nominal stem or verbal root has one of the three tonal types: H(igh), L(ow), 0(zero). High, Low, Falling or Rising tones is assigned to a syllable according to both the tonal type and the total number of syllables in a word.' No stress statement in the abstract; Japanese body chapters not scanned-able here (no jpn tesseract model).
